transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you saw a problem that wasn't yours to fix, and you fixed it anyway.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Our data pipeline was dropping records and no one had noticed because the monitoring was bad. I saw it while debugging something else. I told the data team and they fixed it. I didn't get involved beyond flagging it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What did you do after flagging it?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I moved on to my own tasks. They handled it from there. It was their system after all.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical decision.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: My lead wanted to handle rate limiting in each service individually. I thought a shared middleware layer was cleaner. We discussed it but he decided to go with his approach. I implemented it as he asked.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I've been reading more about distributed systems but I haven't had a specific moment where I was dramatically wrong. I try to stay curious.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What's a weakness you've had to actively work on?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I think I'm pretty good at most things. I sometimes go deep on problems longer than necessary, but I've gotten better at timeboxing. I'm generally pretty self-aware.
